items.title: `Store<List<T: Keyed>>::by_key` scans the list on EVERY read and write through the handle (`keyed_element` / `keyed_write`, store.vl:884-900): a field patch costs O(list length), and one turn patching every row of a 32,000-row list takes 5.3 s
items.status: OPEN - filed 2026-11-05 (the integrator's find, measuring the reactive lens lab against Store)
items.discussion: measured on 0.54.0 in proposal/reactive-lens-lab (src/bench.vl, best of five): rename one row x200 costs 6 ms at 2,089 rows and 25 ms at 32,000; one batch patching `status` on every row costs 28 ms at 2,089 rows and 5,325 ms at 32,000 - the same through handles the rows already hold, so it is the write, not the lookup at the call site. The lens lab's positional table does the same turn in 50 ms and kolt's prototype in 890 ms. kolt itself is not exposed: its records live in HashMaps by id, whose keyed step is one lookup
items.body: by_key's doc says 'the first element whose key is `key`' and both closures it hands `descend` walk the list for the hash. Rec: keep a key -> position index on the sequence node, maintained by the node's own splices (it already records a SeqOp per handle write) and rebuilt on a whole write; `keyed_element` / `keyed_write` consult it and fall back to the scan when it is absent. Pin: the wide turn at 32,000 rows under a ceiling that a scan cannot meet (a count of element visits is steadier than a clock); a differential against the scan for reads after splices, moves and whole writes. Sizing M. Superseded if A185 re-founds Store's lists on the lens (its S6).
